findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the no-exception assertion races with in-flight requests
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the main thread deletes the groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. The reader thread is started with new Thread(...).start() but the reference is discarded and it is never joined. When deletedAll is flipped, the reader may still be blocked inside managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...); if that in-flight request triggers the very NPE/500 this test is meant to catch, the exception is appended to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already executed, so the test passes even though the bug reproduced. The test's outcome is therefore timing-dependent and can silently miss regressions. Keep the Thread reference, join() it (with a timeout) after deletedAll.set(true), and only then assert on caughtExceptions.

findings.title: If a group deletion throws, the polling thread spins forever for the rest of the JVM lifetime
findings.body: deletedAll.set(true) on line 155 is only reached if every managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove() call in the preceding forEach succeeds. If any deletion throws (which is exactly the kind of failure this concurrency test is probing for), the flag is never set and the non-daemon reader thread keeps looping while (!deletedAll.get()) indefinitely, firing REST calls in a tight no-sleep loop and appending every resulting exception to the unbounded CopyOnWriteArrayList caughtExceptions. That leaked thread keeps hammering the server (and growing the list) through the remainder of the test suite, which can destabilize unrelated tests and the CI executor. Wrap the deletion loop in try/finally so the flag is always set, and join the thread.

findings.title: Same concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the three getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The PR fixes getSubGroupsCount() for the case where the group is concurrently deleted (modelSupplier.get() returns null), but the three getSubGroupsStream overloads directly above it (lines 256, 262, and 268) still dereference the supplier result without a null check: return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...). Under the exact same race as issue #40368 — the group is deleted after the cached entry is loaded but before the lazy delegate lookup — modelSupplier.get() returns null and these paths throw a NullPointerException, surfacing as a 500 on endpoints such as GET /admin/realms/{realm}/groups/{id}/children. The same null handling applied in getSubGroupsCount() should be applied (or the method should consistently fall back to getDelegateForUpdate()/an empty stream) in all three overloads.
